name: Coteaux du Lyonnais

known.via: English Wikipedia "Coteaux du Lyonnais AOC" (redirects to "Coteaux du Lyonnais")

limits: For red and rosé wine, Gamay de Bouze and Gamay de Chaudenay together: at most 10%

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
A wine made within weeks of harvest and released at 12:01 am on the third Thursday of November.
The middle tier, from 39 villages in the north of the region. The crus, such as Fleurie, sit above it.

notes: Gamay gives Beaujolais a deep bluish-red color, high acidity, moderate tannin and light to medium body.
The wines smell of blueberries, cherries, raspberries and currants.
Cru Beaujolais typically tastes of sour cherry, black pepper and dried berries, with a note of fresh-cut stone.
Moulin-à-Vent makes the fullest bodied and most powerful Beaujolais.
Beaujolais Nouveau is simple and light bodied, and it long shaped the region's image.

blurb.text: An appellation on the slopes of the Monts du Lyonnais, west of Lyon, between the Beaujolais and Rhône Valley vineyards. Reds and rosés are made from Gamay, and whites from Chardonnay and Aligoté.
